notes: Bit 1's name carries the maker's footnote 1.
Bit 0's name carries the maker's footnote 1.

fields.name: EEAR[9:8]
fields.text: EEPROM address bits 9:8, high part of EEAR. EEAR is undefined at reset; write a valid address before any EEPROM access. On ATmega48A/48PA these bits are unused and must be written 0.

fields.name: EEAR
fields.text: EEPROM address bits 7:0, low part of EEAR: the linear byte address of the EEPROM location to access. EEAR is undefined at reset; write a valid address before any EEPROM access.

fields.name: EEDR
fields.text: EEPROM data: the byte to write to the EEPROM location in EEAR, or the byte read back from that location.

fields.name: EEPM
fields.text: EEPROM programming mode: which action a write of EEPE starts, erase and write together or either one alone. Writes to it are ignored while EEPE is 1; reset returns it to 0b00 unless the EEPROM is busy programming.

fields.name: EERIE
fields.text: EEPROM ready interrupt enable: 1 enables the interrupt when SREG.I is 1, 0 disables it. The interrupt requests continuously while EEPE is 0, and not during an EEPROM write or SPM.

fields.name: EEMPE
fields.text: EEPROM master write enable: while 1, setting EEPE within 4 clock cycles writes the EEPROM at the selected address; while 0, setting EEPE does nothing. Hardware clears it 4 clock cycles after software sets it.

fields.name: EEPE
fields.text: EEPROM write enable: the write strobe. With address and data set up, write EEMPE to 1 (with EEPE 0), then EEPE to 1 within 4 clock cycles; without EEMPE no write happens. Sequence: wait for EEPE 0, wait for SPMCSR.SPMEN 0 (only when a boot loader writes Flash), set EEAR and EEDR (in either order, both optional), set EEMPE, then EEPE. No EEPROM write is possible while the CPU writes Flash. An interrupt between setting EEMPE and EEPE makes the write fail, and an interrupt routine that touches EEAR or EEDR spoils an access it interrupts. Hardware clears EEPE when the write time has passed; setting it halts the CPU for 2 cycles.

fields.name: EERE
fields.text: EEPROM read enable: the read strobe. With EEAR set, write 1 to read; the read takes one instruction, the data is ready at once, and the CPU halts for 4 cycles before the next instruction. Poll EEPE first: while a write runs, neither a read nor a change of EEAR is possible. EEPROM accesses are timed by the calibrated oscillator.

fields.name: GPIOR2
fields.text: General purpose I/O register 2: a byte of storage.

fields.name: GPIOR1

fields.name: GPIOR0

registers.name: OSCCAL
registers.title: Oscillator Calibration Register
notes: Initial value of bits 7:0 printed as Device Specific Calibration Value.

fields.name: CAL
fields.text: Oscillator calibration: trims the calibrated internal RC oscillator. Reset loads the factory value; software may write another to change the frequency, and calibration outside the specified range is not ensured. This oscillator times EEPROM and Flash writes, so their times change with it; above 8.8MHz those writes may fail. CAL7 picks the low (0) or high (1) range, and the ranges overlap (0x7F is faster than 0x80); CAL6:0 tunes within the range, 0x00 slowest and 0x7F fastest.

registers.name: CLKPR

notes: Initial value of bits 3:0 printed as See Bit Description.

fields.name: CLKPCE
fields.text: Clock prescaler change enable: write 1, with every other CLKPR bit 0 in the same write, to allow a change of CLKPS. Hardware clears it 4 cycles later or when CLKPS is written; writing it again in that time neither extends nor clears it.

fields.name: CLKPS
fields.text: Clock prescaler select: the division factor from the selected clock source to the system clock, writable at run time; it slows every synchronous peripheral too. Reset value comes from the CKDIV8 fuse: 0b0000 when unprogrammed, 0b0011 (divide by 8) when programmed, and the part ships with CKDIV8 programmed. Any value may be written whatever the fuse.

fields.name: SM
fields.text: Sleep mode select: which of the five sleep modes SLEEP enters. Standby mode is for external crystals or resonators.

fields.name: SE
fields.text: Sleep enable: must be 1 for SLEEP to put the MCU to sleep; set it just before SLEEP and clear it on wake-up.

fields.name: BODS
fields.text: BOD sleep: 1 turns the BOD off during sleep. Set it by a timed sequence: write BODS and BODSE both 1, then within 4 clock cycles write BODS 1 with BODSE 0. It takes effect 3 clock cycles after being set, SLEEP must run while it is active, and it clears itself after 3 clock cycles.

fields.name: BODSE
fields.text: BOD sleep enable: allows BODS to be set in its timed sequence. BODS and BODSE exist only on the picoPower parts (ATmega48PA/88PA/168PA/328P).

fields.name: PRTWI
fields.text: Power reduction TWI: 1 stops the TWI clock; reinitialize the TWI after waking it.

fields.name: PRTIM2
fields.text: Power reduction Timer/Counter2: 1 shuts down Timer/Counter2 in synchronous mode (AS2 = 0); when re-enabled it carries on as before.

fields.name: PRTIM0
fields.text: Power reduction Timer/Counter0: 1 shuts down Timer/Counter0; when re-enabled it carries on as before.

fields.name: PRTIM1
fields.text: Power reduction Timer/Counter1: 1 shuts down Timer/Counter1; when re-enabled it carries on as before.

fields.name: PRSPI
fields.text: Power reduction SPI: 1 stops the SPI clock; reinitialize the SPI after waking it. Leave at 0 when using debugWIRE.

fields.name: PRUSART0
fields.text: Power reduction USART0: 1 stops the USART clock; reinitialize the USART after waking it.

fields.name: PRADC
fields.text: Power reduction ADC: 1 shuts down the ADC, which must be disabled first; the analog comparator then cannot use the ADC input multiplexer.

registers.name: MCUSR
registers.title: MCU Status Register
notes: Initial value of bits 3:0 printed as See Bit Description.

fields.name: WDRF
fields.text: Watchdog reset flag: a watchdog reset sets it; a power-on reset or a write of 0 clears it.

fields.name: BORF
fields.text: Brown-out reset flag: a brown-out reset sets it; a power-on reset or a write of 0 clears it.

fields.name: EXTRF
fields.text: External reset flag: an external reset sets it; a power-on reset or a write of 0 clears it.

fields.name: PORF
fields.text: Power-on reset flag: set by a power-on reset; cleared only by writing 0. Read and clear MCUSR early in the program so the flags show the source of the next reset.

fields.name: WDIF
fields.text: Watchdog interrupt flag: set on a watchdog time-out when the watchdog is configured for interrupt. Cleared by hardware when its vector runs, or by writing 1. The interrupt runs when SREG.I and WDIE are 1.

fields.name: WDIE
fields.text: Watchdog interrupt enable: with SREG.I set, 1 enables the watchdog interrupt. With WDE 0 the watchdog is in interrupt mode; with WDE 1 it is in interrupt and system reset mode, where the first time-out sets WDIF and running its vector clears WDIE and WDIF, which puts the watchdog in system reset mode. To stay in the combined mode, set WDIE again after each interrupt, not inside the interrupt routine; a second time-out before the interrupt runs resets the system. WDTON 0 is programmed, 1 unprogrammed.

fields.name: WDP3
fields.text: Watchdog timer prescaler bit 3: with WDP2:0, sets the watchdog prescaling and time-out while it runs.

fields.name: WDCE
fields.text: Watchdog change enable: must be 1 to clear WDE or change the prescaler bits in their timed sequence; hardware clears it 4 clock cycles after it is written to 1.

fields.name: WDE
fields.text: Watchdog system reset enable: forced to 1 while MCUSR.WDRF is 1, so WDRF must be cleared before WDE can be. This keeps resets repeating while the fault lasts and gives a safe start-up after it.

fields.name: WDP2
fields.text: Watchdog timer prescaler bit 2: with WDP3 and WDP1:0, sets the watchdog prescaling and time-out while it runs.

fields.name: WDP1
fields.text: Watchdog timer prescaler bit 1: with WDP3:2 and WDP0, sets the watchdog prescaling and time-out while it runs.

fields.name: WDP0
fields.text: Watchdog timer prescaler bit 0: with WDP3:1, sets the watchdog prescaling and time-out while it runs.

fields.name: IVSEL
fields.text: Interrupt vector select: 0 puts the interrupt vectors at the start of Flash, 1 at the start of the boot loader section, whose address the BOOTSZ fuses set. To change it: write IVCE 1, then within 4 cycles write the new IVSEL with IVCE 0. Interrupts are off from the cycle IVCE is set until after the instruction that writes IVSEL, or for 4 cycles if IVSEL is not written; SREG.I is not changed. With vectors in the boot section and BLB02 programmed, interrupts are off while running from the application section; with vectors in the application section and BLB12 programmed, they are off while running from the boot section.

fields.name: IVCE
fields.text: Interrupt vector change enable: write 1 to allow IVSEL to be changed. Hardware clears it 4 cycles after the write, or when IVSEL is written. Setting it turns interrupts off, as for IVSEL.

fields.name: ISC1
fields.text: Interrupt sense control 1: which level or edge on INT1 triggers external interrupt 1, which runs when SREG.I and its mask bit are set. The pin is sampled before edge detection. In edge or toggle mode a pulse longer than one clock period triggers it, shorter ones may not; in low-level mode the level must last until the current instruction ends.

fields.name: ISC0
fields.text: Interrupt sense control 0: which level or edge on INT0 triggers external interrupt 0, which runs when SREG.I and its mask bit are set. The pin is sampled before edge detection. In edge or toggle mode a pulse longer than one clock period triggers it, shorter ones may not; in low-level mode the level must last until the current instruction ends.

fields.name: INT1
fields.text: External interrupt 1 enable: with SREG.I set, 1 enables the INT1 pin interrupt, triggered as EICRA.ISC1 selects; pin activity triggers it even when INT1 is an output. It runs from the INT1 vector.

fields.name: INT0
fields.text: External interrupt 0 enable: with SREG.I set, 1 enables the INT0 pin interrupt, triggered as EICRA.ISC0 selects; pin activity triggers it even when INT0 is an output. It runs from the INT0 vector.

fields.name: INTF1
fields.text: External interrupt flag 1: set when an edge or change on INT1 requests an interrupt; with SREG.I and EIMSK.INT1 set the MCU jumps to its vector. Cleared when the routine runs or by writing 1; always 0 while INT1 is set for level interrupt.

fields.name: INTF0
fields.text: External interrupt flag 0: set when an edge or change on INT0 requests an interrupt; with SREG.I and EIMSK.INT0 set the MCU jumps to its vector. Cleared when the routine runs or by writing 1; always 0 while INT0 is set for level interrupt.

fields.name: PCIE2
fields.text: Pin change interrupt enable 2: with SREG.I set, 1 enables pin change interrupt 2, so a change on any PCINT[23:16] pin enabled in PCMSK2 triggers it; it runs from the PCI2 vector.

fields.name: PCIE1
fields.text: Pin change interrupt enable 1: with SREG.I set, 1 enables pin change interrupt 1, so a change on any PCINT[14:8] pin enabled in PCMSK1 triggers it; it runs from the PCI1 vector.

fields.name: PCIE0
fields.text: Pin change interrupt enable 0: with SREG.I set, 1 enables pin change interrupt 0, so a change on any PCINT[7:0] pin enabled in PCMSK0 triggers it; it runs from the PCI0 vector.

fields.name: PCIF2
fields.text: Pin change interrupt flag 2: set when a change on a PCINT[23:16] pin requests an interrupt; with SREG.I and PCICR.PCIE2 set the MCU jumps to its vector. Cleared when the routine runs or by writing 1.

fields.name: PCIF1
fields.text: Pin change interrupt flag 1: set when a change on a PCINT[14:8] pin requests an interrupt; with SREG.I and PCICR.PCIE1 set the MCU jumps to its vector. Cleared when the routine runs or by writing 1.

fields.name: PCIF0
fields.text: Pin change interrupt flag 0: set when a change on a PCINT[7:0] pin requests an interrupt; with SREG.I and PCICR.PCIE0 set the MCU jumps to its vector. Cleared when the routine runs or by writing 1.

fields.name: PCINT[23:16]
fields.text: Pin change enable mask PCINT[23:16]: each bit at 1, with PCICR.PCIE2 set, enables the pin change interrupt on its I/O pin; at 0 that pin's interrupt is off.

fields.name: PCINT[14:8]
fields.text: Pin change enable mask PCINT[14:8]: each bit at 1, with PCICR.PCIE1 set, enables the pin change interrupt on its I/O pin; at 0 that pin's interrupt is off.

fields.name: PCINT
fields.text: Pin change enable mask PCINT[7:0]: each bit at 1, with PCICR.PCIE0 set, enables the pin change interrupt on its I/O pin; at 0 that pin's interrupt is off.

fields.name: WGM2
fields.text: Waveform generation mode, low bits: with TCCR2B.WGM22, selects the counting sequence, the source of TOP and the waveform type: normal, clear timer on compare match (CTC), or one of two PWM modes. MAX is 0xFF and BOTTOM 0x00.

registers.name: TCCR2B
registers.title: Timer/Counter Control Register B
notes: The settings of WGM22 are carried on TCCR2A.WGM2, which holds the low bits.

fields.name: FOC2A
fields.text: Force output compare A: writing 1 forces an immediate compare match on the waveform generator, changing OC2A as COM2A1:0 are set now. Active only in non-PWM modes; write it 0 when writing TCCR2B in a PWM mode. It is a strobe: it raises no interrupt, does not clear the timer in CTC mode with OCR2A as TOP, and always reads 0.

fields.name: FOC2B
fields.text: Force output compare B: writing 1 forces an immediate compare match on the waveform generator, changing OC2B as COM2B1:0 are set now. Active only in non-PWM modes; write it 0 when writing TCCR2B in a PWM mode. It is a strobe: it raises no interrupt, does not clear the timer in CTC mode with OCR2B as TOP, and always reads 0.

fields.name: WGM22
fields.text: Waveform generation mode bit 2: the high bit of WGM2, with TCCR2A.WGM21:0.

fields.name: CS2
fields.text: Clock select: the Timer/Counter2 clock source. With an external pin source, edges on the T0 pin clock the counter even when the pin is an output, so software can drive the count.

fields.name: TCNT2
fields.text: Timer/Counter2 count value.

fields.name: OCR2A
fields.text: Output compare register A value for Timer/Counter2.

fields.name: OCR2B
fields.text: Output compare register B value for Timer/Counter2.

fields.name: OCIE2B
fields.text: Output compare match B interrupt enable: with SREG.I set, 1 enables the Timer/Counter2 compare match B interrupt, which runs when TIFR2.OCF2B is set.

fields.name: OCIE2A
fields.text: Output compare match A interrupt enable: with SREG.I set, 1 enables the Timer/Counter2 compare match A interrupt, which runs when TIFR2.OCF2A is set.

fields.name: TOIE2
fields.text: Overflow interrupt enable: with SREG.I set, 1 enables the Timer/Counter2 overflow interrupt, which runs when TIFR2.TOV2 is set.

fields.name: OCF2B
fields.text: Output compare flag 2 B: set when TCNT2 matches OCR2B. Cleared by hardware when its vector runs, or by writing 1. The interrupt runs when SREG.I, OCIE2B and OCF2B are all 1.

fields.name: OCF2A
fields.text: Output compare flag 2 A: set when TCNT2 matches OCR2A. Cleared by hardware when its vector runs, or by writing 1. The interrupt runs when SREG.I, OCIE2A and OCF2A are all 1.

fields.name: TOV2
fields.text: Overflow flag: set when Timer/Counter2 overflows; in PWM mode, when it reverses direction at 0x00. Cleared by hardware when its vector runs, or by writing 1. The interrupt runs when SREG.I, TIMSK2.TOIE2 and TOV2 are all 1.

fields.name: EXCLK
fields.text: Enable external clock input: with the asynchronous clock selected, 1 enables the TOSC1 input buffer so an external clock replaces the 32kHz crystal. Write it before selecting asynchronous operation; the crystal oscillator runs only while it is 0.

fields.name: AS2
fields.text: Asynchronous Timer/Counter2: 0 clocks Timer/Counter2 from clkI/O, 1 from a crystal oscillator on TOSC1. Changing it may corrupt TCNT2, OCR2A, OCR2B, TCCR2A and TCCR2B.

fields.name: TCN2UB
fields.text: TCNT2 update busy: in asynchronous operation, set when TCNT2 is written and cleared by hardware once TCNT2 is updated from its temporary register; 0 means TCNT2 can take a new value.

fields.name: OCR2AUB
fields.text: OCR2A update busy: in asynchronous operation, set when OCR2A is written and cleared by hardware once OCR2A is updated from its temporary register; 0 means OCR2A can take a new value.

fields.name: OCR2BUB
fields.text: OCR2B update busy: in asynchronous operation, set when OCR2B is written and cleared by hardware once OCR2B is updated from its temporary register; 0 means OCR2B can take a new value.

fields.name: TCR2AUB
fields.text: TCCR2A update busy: in asynchronous operation, set when TCCR2A is written and cleared by hardware once TCCR2A is updated from its temporary register; 0 means TCCR2A can take a new value.

fields.name: TCR2BUB
fields.text: TCCR2B update busy: in asynchronous operation, set when TCCR2B is written and cleared by hardware once TCCR2B is updated from its temporary register; 0 means TCCR2B can take a new value. A write to one of the five Timer/Counter2 registers whose busy flag is still 1 may corrupt it and cause an unintended interrupt. Reading TCNT2 gives the live count; reading OCR2A, OCR2B, TCCR2A or TCCR2B gives the temporary register.

fields.name: TSM
fields.text: Timer/counter synchronization mode.

fields.name: PSRASY
fields.text: Prescaler reset Timer/Counter2: 1 resets the Timer/Counter2 prescaler. Hardware clears it at once, except that in asynchronous mode it stays 1 until the reset is done, and it is not cleared while TSM is 1.

fields.name: PSRSYNC
fields.text: Prescaler reset for Timer/Counter1 and Timer/Counter0.

fields.name: SPIE
fields.text: SPI interrupt enable: the SPI interrupt runs when SPSR.SPIF and SREG.I are both 1.

fields.name: SPE
fields.text: SPI enable: 1 enables the SPI; required for any SPI operation.

fields.name: DORD
fields.text: Data order: 1 sends the LSB of the data word first, 0 the MSB first.

fields.name: MSTR
fields.text: Master/slave select: 1 selects master, 0 slave. If SS is an input and is pulled low while MSTR is 1, MSTR clears and SPSR.SPIF sets; MSTR must then be set again to return to master.

fields.name: CPOL
fields.text: Clock polarity: 1 holds SCK high when idle, 0 low.

fields.name: CPHA
fields.text: Clock phase: picks whether the first (leading) or the last (trailing) SCK edge samples the data.

fields.name: SPR
fields.text: SPI clock rate select: with SPSR.SPI2X, sets the SCK rate from fosc when master; no effect in slave mode.

registers.name: SPSR
registers.title: SPI Status Register
notes: The settings of SPI2X are carried on SPCR.SPR, which holds the low bits.

fields.name: SPIF
fields.text: SPI interrupt flag: set when a transfer completes, and also when SS is an input pulled low in master mode; raises an interrupt if SPCR.SPIE and global interrupts are on. Cleared by hardware when its vector runs, or by reading SPSR with SPIF set and then accessing SPDR.

fields.name: WCOL
fields.text: Write collision flag: set when SPDR is written during a transfer. Cleared, with SPIF, by reading SPSR with WCOL set and then accessing SPDR. SPSR bits 5:1 are reserved and read 0.

fields.name: SPI2X
fields.text: Double SPI speed: in master mode, 1 doubles the SCK frequency, giving a minimum SCK period of two CPU clocks. As slave, operation is ensured only up to fosc/4. The SPI is also used for downloading and uploading program memory and EEPROM.

fields.name: SPDR
fields.text: SPI data register.

fields.name: RXC0
fields.text: USART receive complete: 1 while the receive buffer holds unread data, 0 when it is empty. Disabling the receiver flushes the buffer and clears it. Can raise the receive complete interrupt (RXCIE0).

fields.name: TXC0
fields.text: USART transmit complete: set when the whole frame has left the transmit shift register and no new data is in UDR0. Cleared when the transmit complete interrupt runs, or by writing 1. Can raise the transmit complete interrupt (TXCIE0).

fields.name: UDRE0
fields.text: USART data register empty: 1 when UDR0 is empty and can be written. Set after reset to show the transmitter is ready. Can raise the data register empty interrupt (UDRIE0).

fields.name: FE0
fields.text: Frame error: 1 when the character waiting next in the receive buffer arrived with a zero first stop bit; 0 when that stop bit was one. Valid until UDR0 is read. Write 0 when writing UCSR0A.

fields.name: DOR0
fields.text: Data overrun: 1 when both receive buffer places hold characters, a third waits in the shift register, and yet another start bit is seen. Valid until UDR0 is read. Write 0 when writing UCSR0A.

fields.name: UPE0
fields.text: USART parity error: 1 when the character waiting next in the receive buffer arrived with bad parity while checking was on (UPM01 = 1). Valid until UDR0 is read. Write 0 when writing UCSR0A.

fields.name: U2X0
fields.text: Double the USART transmission speed: in asynchronous mode, 1 cuts the baud rate divisor from 16 to 8, doubling the rate. Write 0 in synchronous mode.

fields.name: MPCM0
fields.text: Multi-processor communication mode: 1 makes the receiver ignore every incoming frame that carries no address information. The transmitter is not affected.

fields.name: RXCIE0
fields.text: RX complete interrupt enable: 1 enables the receive complete interrupt, raised when this bit, SREG.I and UCSR0A.RXC0 are all 1.

fields.name: TXCIE0
fields.text: TX complete interrupt enable: 1 enables the transmit complete interrupt, raised when this bit, SREG.I and UCSR0A.TXC0 are all 1.

fields.name: UDRIE0
fields.text: USART data register empty interrupt enable: 1 enables the data register empty interrupt, raised when this bit, SREG.I and UCSR0A.UDRE0 are all 1.

fields.name: RXEN0
fields.text: Receiver enable: 1 enables the receiver, which takes over the RxD0 pin. Disabling it flushes the receive buffer, making FE0, DOR0 and UPE0 invalid.

fields.name: TXEN0
fields.text: Transmitter enable: 1 enables the transmitter, which takes over the TxD0 pin. Writing 0 takes effect only once the shift register and transmit buffer are empty; the pin then returns to the port.

fields.name: UCSZ02
fields.text: Character size bit 2: with UCSR0C.UCSZ01:0, sets the number of data bits per frame for receiver and transmitter.

fields.name: RXB80

fields.name: TXB80

fields.name: UPM0

fields.name: USBS0
fields.text: Stop bit select: how many stop bits the transmitter sends; the receiver ignores it.

fields.name: UCSZ0
fields.text: Character size bits 1:0: with UCSR0B.UCSZ02, set the number of data bits per frame for receiver and transmitter.

fields.name: UCPOL0

fields.text: Clock polarity: the polarity of XCK0; with UCPHA0 it sets the data transfer timing.

fields.name: TWBR7
fields.text: Bit 7 of the bit rate generator's division factor; the generator divides down to the SCL clock in Master modes.

fields.name: TWBR6
fields.text: Bit 6 of the bit rate generator's division factor; the generator divides down to the SCL clock in Master modes.

fields.name: TWBR5
fields.text: Bit 5 of the bit rate generator's division factor; the generator divides down to the SCL clock in Master modes.

fields.name: TWBR4
fields.text: Bit 4 of the bit rate generator's division factor; the generator divides down to the SCL clock in Master modes.

fields.name: TWBR3
fields.text: Bit 3 of the bit rate generator's division factor; the generator divides down to the SCL clock in Master modes.

fields.name: TWBR2
fields.text: Bit 2 of the bit rate generator's division factor; the generator divides down to the SCL clock in Master modes.

fields.name: TWBR1
fields.text: Bit 1 of the bit rate generator's division factor; the generator divides down to the SCL clock in Master modes.

fields.name: TWBR0
fields.text: Bit 0 of the bit rate generator's division factor; the generator divides down to the SCL clock in Master modes.

fields.name: TWINT
fields.text: Hardware sets TWINT when the TWI ends its current job and waits for software; with TWIE and the SREG I-bit set, the TWI interrupt vector is taken. SCL low is held stretched while TWINT is set. Software clears it by writing 1; running the interrupt routine does not clear it. Clearing it starts the TWI, so TWAR, TWSR and TWDR accesses must finish first.

fields.name: TWEA
fields.text: Writing 1 makes the device send ACK when its own slave address arrives, when a general call arrives with TWAR.TWGCE set, or when a data byte arrives in Master Receiver or Slave Receiver mode. Writing 0 detaches the device from the bus for a time; writing 1 again resumes address recognition.

fields.name: TWSTA
fields.text: Write 1 to become bus master: the TWI sends a START once the bus is free, otherwise waits for a STOP and then sends one. Software must clear TWSTA after the START has gone out.

fields.name: TWSTO
fields.text: In Master mode, writing 1 sends a STOP on the bus; the bit clears itself once the STOP is done. In Slave mode, writing 1 recovers from an error with no STOP sent: the TWI goes back to unaddressed Slave mode and lets SCL and SDA go high impedance.

fields.name: TWWC
fields.text: Set when TWDR is written while TWINT is low. Cleared by writing TWDR while TWINT is high.

fields.name: TWEN
fields.text: Writing 1 turns the TWI on: it takes over the SCL and SDA pins and enables their slew-rate limiters and spike filters. Writing 0 turns it off and ends any transfer at once, whatever is in progress.

fields.name: TWIE
fields.text: With this bit at 1 and the SREG I-bit set, the TWI interrupt is requested for as long as TWINT is high.

fields.name: TWS
fields.text: Five-bit status of the TWI logic and the bus. A read of TWSR also returns the two prescaler bits; masking them to zero makes the status independent of the prescaler.

fields.name: TWPS
fields.text: Bit rate prescaler, read/write; its value enters the bit rate equation.

fields.name: TWD
fields.text: Holds the next byte to send on the bus, or the last byte received from it.

fields.name: TWA
fields.text: Seven-bit slave address of the TWI.

fields.name: TWGCE
fields.text: When set, the TWI recognises a general call on the bus.

fields.name: TWAM
fields.text: Seven-bit mask for the slave address in TWAR: a TWAM bit at one makes the address match logic skip the comparison of that incoming address bit with its TWAR bit.

registers.name: ADCSRB
registers.title: ADC Control and Status Register B

fields.name: ACME
fields.text: With this bit at 1 and the ADC off (ADCSRA.ADEN = 0), the ADC multiplexer picks the comparator's negative input. At 0, AIN1 is the negative input.

fields.name: ADTS2
fields.text: ADC auto trigger source, bit 2.

fields.name: ADTS1
fields.text: ADC auto trigger source, bit 1.

fields.name: ADTS0
fields.text: ADC auto trigger source, bit 0.

registers.name: ACSR
registers.title: Analog Comparator Control and Status Register
notes: Initial value of bit 5 printed as N/A.

fields.name: ACD
fields.text: Writing 1 removes power from the comparator, and may be done at any time; this lowers consumption in Active and Idle mode. Clear ACIE before changing ACD, or an interrupt can occur on the change.

fields.name: ACBG
fields.text: When set, a fixed bandgap reference takes the place of the comparator's positive input; when clear, AIN0 is the positive input. The bandgap takes time to settle, and the first conversion before it has settled can be wrong.

fields.name: ACO
fields.text: Comparator output after synchronisation, which delays it by 1 to 2 clock cycles.

fields.name: ACI
fields.text: Hardware sets ACI when a comparator output event matches the mode in ACIS1:0. The interrupt runs when ACIE and the SREG I-bit are set. Cleared by hardware on entering the interrupt vector, or by writing 1.

fields.name: ACIE
fields.text: With ACIE at 1 and the SREG I-bit set, the comparator interrupt is on; at 0 it is off.

fields.name: ACIC
fields.text: At 1, the comparator output drives the Timer/Counter1 input capture front end directly, using its noise canceler and edge select. At 0 there is no link between them. TIMSK1.ICIE1 must be set for the comparator to raise the Timer/Counter1 Input Capture interrupt.

fields.name: ACIS
fields.text: Selects which comparator events raise the comparator interrupt. Clear ACIE before changing these bits, or an interrupt can occur on the change.

fields.name: AIN1D
fields.text: Writing 1 disables the digital input buffer on AIN1, and its PIN register bit then always reads 0. Set it when the pin carries an analog signal and its digital input is unused, to save power in the buffer.

fields.name: AIN0D
fields.text: Writing one turns off the digital input buffer on the AIN0 pin; while set, the matching PIN register bit reads zero. Setting it saves power in that buffer when the pin carries an analog signal and its digital input is unused.

fields.name: REFS
fields.text: Selects the ADC voltage reference. A change during a conversion takes effect only when that conversion ends (ADCSRA.ADIF set). The internal reference choices are not to be used while an external voltage is applied on AREF.

values.text: AVCC, with an external capacitor on AREF.
Internal 1.1V reference, with an external capacitor on AREF.

fields.name: ADLAR
fields.text: Write 1 to left-adjust the conversion result in the ADC data register; at 0 it is right-adjusted. A change takes effect on the data register at once, even during a conversion.

fields.name: MUX
fields.text: Selects the analog input connected to the ADC. A change during a conversion takes effect only when that conversion ends (ADCSRA.ADIF set).

registers.name: ADCSRA
registers.title: ADC Control and Status Register A

fields.name: ADEN
fields.text: Write 1 to turn the ADC on, 0 to turn it off; turning it off during a conversion ends that conversion.

fields.name: ADSC
fields.text: Write 1 to start each conversion in Single Conversion mode, or the first one in Free Running mode. The first conversion after the ADC is enabled, or with ADSC written together with the enable, initialises the ADC and takes 25 ADC clock cycles instead of 13. Reads 1 while a conversion runs and 0 once it is done; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: ADATE
fields.text: Writing 1 enables auto triggering: a conversion starts on a rising edge of the trigger signal chosen by ADCSRB.ADTS.

fields.name: ADIF
fields.text: Set once a conversion finishes and the result registers hold it. The Conversion Complete interrupt runs when ADIE and the SREG I-bit are set. Cleared by hardware on entering the interrupt vector, or by writing 1. A read-modify-write of ADCSRA, SBI and CBI included, can disable a pending interrupt.

fields.name: ADIE
fields.text: With this bit at 1 and the SREG I-bit set, the ADC Conversion Complete interrupt is on.

fields.name: ADPS
fields.text: Sets the division factor from the system clock to the ADC input clock.

fields.name: ADC9
fields.text: Result bit 9, right-adjusted (ADLAR = 0).

registers.name: ADCSRB
registers.title: ADC Control and Status Register B

fields.name: ACME
fields.text: Analog comparator multiplexer enable.

fields.name: ADTS
fields.text: With ADCSRA.ADATE at 1, picks the source whose interrupt flag's rising edge starts a conversion; with ADATE clear the setting does nothing. Switching from a cleared source to a set one makes a rising edge, which starts a conversion if ADCSRA.ADEN is set. Switching to Free Running (0) makes no trigger, even with the ADC interrupt flag set.

fields.name: ADC5D
fields.text: Writing 1 disables the digital input buffer on ADC5, and its PIN register bit then always reads 0. Set it when the pin carries an analog signal and its digital input is unused, to save power in the buffer. ADC7 and ADC6 have no digital input buffer and no such bit.

fields.name: ADC4D
fields.text: Writing one turns off the digital input buffer on the ADC4 pin; while set, the matching PIN register bit reads zero. Setting it saves power in that buffer when the pin carries an analog signal and its digital input is unused. ADC7 and ADC6 have no digital input buffer and no such bit.

fields.name: ADC3D
fields.text: Writing one turns off the digital input buffer on the ADC3 pin; while set, the matching PIN register bit reads zero. Setting it saves power in that buffer when the pin carries an analog signal and its digital input is unused. ADC7 and ADC6 have no digital input buffer and no such bit.

fields.name: ADC2D
fields.text: Writing one turns off the digital input buffer on the ADC2 pin; while set, the matching PIN register bit reads zero. Setting it saves power in that buffer when the pin carries an analog signal and its digital input is unused. ADC7 and ADC6 have no digital input buffer and no such bit.

fields.name: ADC1D
fields.text: Writing one turns off the digital input buffer on the ADC1 pin; while set, the matching PIN register bit reads zero. Setting it saves power in that buffer when the pin carries an analog signal and its digital input is unused. ADC7 and ADC6 have no digital input buffer and no such bit.

fields.name: ADC0D
fields.text: Writing one turns off the digital input buffer on the ADC0 pin; while set, the matching PIN register bit reads zero. Setting it saves power in that buffer when the pin carries an analog signal and its digital input is unused. ADC7 and ADC6 have no digital input buffer and no such bit.

registers.name: SPMCSR
registers.title: Store Program Memory Control and Status Register

fields.name: SPMIE
fields.text: With this bit at one and the SREG I-bit set, the SPM ready interrupt is enabled; it runs for as long as SPMCSR.SPMEN is zero. No interrupt is raised during an EEPROM write or an SPM.

fields.name: RWWSB
fields.text: Kept for compatibility with Read-While-Write devices; on ATmega48A/48PA it always reads zero.

fields.name: SIGRD
fields.text: Set together with SPMEN, it makes an LPM within the next three clock cycles load a signature row byte into the destination register. Once both bits are set, an SPM in the following four cycles does nothing. Reserved for future use; not to be used.

fields.name: RWWSRE
fields.text: On ATmega48A/48PA this bit does a part of what it does on ATmega88A/88PA/168A/168PA/328/328P. Writing it while the temporary page buffer is being filled clears that buffer and its data is lost.

fields.name: BLBSET
fields.text: On ATmega48A/48PA this bit does a part of what it does on ATmega88A/88PA/168A/168PA/328/328P. Once BLBSET and SPMEN are both set, an LPM in the following three cycles loads the Lock bits or the Fuse bits, chosen by Z0 of the Z-pointer, into the destination register.

fields.name: PGWRT
fields.text: Set together with SPMEN, it makes an SPM in the following four clock cycles program the page given by the upper part of the Z-pointer from the temporary buffer; R1 and R0 are not used. It clears itself when the write ends or when no SPM comes within four clock cycles. The CPU stops for the whole Page Write.

fields.name: PGERS
fields.text: Set together with SPMEN, it makes an SPM within the next four clock cycles erase the page given by the upper part of the Z-pointer; R1 and R0 are not used. It clears itself when the erase ends or when no SPM comes within four clock cycles. The CPU stops for the whole operation.

fields.name: SPMEN
fields.text: Enables the SPM instruction for the following four clock cycles. Written with RWWSRE, BLBSET, PGWRT or PGERS, it gives the next SPM that bit's operation; written alone, the next SPM stores R1:R0 in the temporary page buffer at the Z-pointer address, with the Z-pointer LSB unused. It clears itself when the SPM completes or when no SPM comes within four clock cycles, and stays at one through a Page Erase or Page Write until it ends. A write to the lower five bits other than 10001, 01001, 00101, 00011 or 00001 does nothing.

registers.name: SPMCSR
registers.title: Store Program Memory Control and Status Register

fields.name: SPMIE
fields.text: With this bit at one and the SREG I-bit set, the SPM ready interrupt is enabled; it runs for as long as SPMCSR.SPMEN is zero.

fields.name: RWWSB
fields.text: Set by hardware when a self-programming erase or write of the RWW section starts; while set, that section is not accessible. Cleared by writing RWWSRE to one after the operation has finished, or on its own when a page load starts.

fields.name: SIGRD
fields.text: Set together with SPMEN, it makes an LPM within the next three clock cycles load a signature row byte into the destination register. Once both bits are set, an SPM in the following four cycles does nothing. Reserved for future use; not to be used.

fields.name: RWWSRE
fields.text: A self-programming erase or write of the RWW section blocks reads of that section and sets RWWSB. Once programming has finished (SPMEN zero), writing RWWSRE with SPMEN makes an SPM within the next four clock cycles open the RWW section again; this cannot be done while SPMEN is set. Writing it during a Flash load aborts the load and the loaded data is lost.

fields.name: BLBSET
fields.text: Set together with SPMEN, it makes an SPM within the next four clock cycles set the Boot Lock and Memory Lock bits from R0; R1 and the Z-pointer address are not used. It clears itself when the Lock bits are set or when no SPM comes within four clock cycles. Once BLBSET and SPMEN are both set, an LPM in the following three cycles loads the Lock bits or the Fuse bits, chosen by Z0 of the Z-pointer, into the destination register.

fields.name: PGWRT
fields.text: Set together with SPMEN, it makes an SPM in the following four clock cycles program the page given by the upper part of the Z-pointer from the temporary buffer; R1 and R0 are not used. It clears itself when the write ends or when no SPM comes within four clock cycles. The CPU stops for the whole Page Write when the NRWW section is the target.

fields.name: PGERS
fields.text: Set together with SPMEN, it makes an SPM within the next four clock cycles erase the page given by the upper part of the Z-pointer; R1 and R0 are not used. It clears itself when the erase ends or when no SPM comes within four clock cycles. The CPU stops for the whole operation when the NRWW section is the target.

fields.name: SPMEN
fields.text: Enables the SPM instruction for the following four clock cycles. Written with RWWSRE, BLBSET, PGWRT or PGERS, it gives the next SPM that bit's operation; written alone, the next SPM stores R1:R0 in the temporary page buffer at the Z-pointer address, with the Z-pointer LSB unused. It clears itself when the SPM completes or when no SPM comes within four clock cycles, and stays at one through a Page Erase or Page Write until it ends. A write to the lower five bits other than 10001, 01001, 00101, 00011 or 00001 does nothing.
